papers.title: Near Resonance, Less Ordered: Radius and Mass Ordering in Compact Multi-planet Systems
papers.abstract: Compact multi-planet systems exhibit a tendency for planetary radii to follow ordered sequences with orbital position, suggesting that these non-random patterns preserve a fossil record of their formation. Here, we investigate whether ordering of planet radii and masses with orbital period is related to proximity to mean-motion resonances. We compare near-resonant and non-resonant systems using complementary rank- and inversion-based measures of ordering, while accounting for differences in planet multiplicity and uncertainties in the measured planetary properties. We find that radii and masses are less monotonically ordered in near-resonant systems than in non-resonant systems, with the primary radius analysis providing stronger evidence than the mass analysis. This result is opposite to the naive expectation that dynamical instabilities should erase the primordial ordering of initially resonant systems and leave non-resonant systems in a more disordered state.

papers.title: A Universal Ratio Linking Cosmic Expansion and the Growth of Structure
papers.abstract: We identify a universal relation between the onset of cosmic acceleration ($z_t$) and the turnover ($z_{\rm pk}$) of the linear growth observable $f\sigma_{8}$. In a spatially flat $\Lambda$CDM Universe, these two redshifts obey $R \equiv (1+z_t)/(1+z_{\rm pk}) = 1.1596$, independent of the present matter fraction and the overall expansion and growth normalisations. This provides a new consistency test for $\Lambda$CDM, linking both background and growth dynamics. We further establish the conditions under which this extends to broader classes of dark energy and modified gravity theories.

papers.title: oMEGACat-JWST I.: Project description and photometric data release
papers.abstract: Omega Centauri (NGC 5139, $\omega$ Cen) is the most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way and the likely stripped nucleus of an accreted dwarf galaxy. Extensive HST observations have uncovered many of its peculiar features, including complex subpopulations and kinematic evidence for an intermediate-mass black hole via central fast-moving stars. High-precision astrometric follow-up is essential to constrain the orbits of these stars. We present oMEGACat-JWST, a deep photometric and astrometric catalog of $\omega$ Cen's core and surroundings that extends our previous oMEGACat efforts to near-infrared wavelengths. The superior sensitivity and angular resolution of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide significant astrometric and photometric improvements, particularly for faint stars. Our catalog is based on a custom reduction of NIRCam and NIRISS imaging across three JWST programs extending out to two half-light radii (10'). In total, our catalog contains approximately 677 000 sources. In the region overlapping with oMEGACat, we achieve high relative completeness (> 90% of HST sources recovered) while detecting over 86 000 new sources below HST's detection limit. Astrometric tests demonstrate a single-image precision as good as 0.5% of a NIRCam pixel (0.15 mas) at mF115W=18; at mF115W=23 the precision is still 1 mas. Color-magnitude diagrams based on our data show the well-known split between the primordial Helium and the Helium enriched populations and are particularly sensitive to light-element (CNO) variations of faint stars. oMEGACat-JWST provides the most complete photometric catalog of $\omega$ Cen's core to date. Combined with HST data, it enables multi-wavelength subpopulation analyses. Together with future monitoring observations, its high astrometric precision will improve our understanding of the kinematics of the central fast-moving stars in $\omega$ Cen.

papers.title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
papers.abstract: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $\Lambda_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $\epsilon_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Its pressure is suppressed relative to both the noninteracting $ud+e$ gas and the representative MIT bag-model prediction. Although the running strong coupling decreases with increasing quark chemical potential, its central value in maximum-mass configurations correlates positively with $M_{\max}$, indicating stronger coupling and reduced perturbative reliability toward the high-mass end. Notably, the squared speed of sound remains nearly constant, varying from $c_s^2\simeq0.321$ to $0.324$ between canonical and maximum-mass configurations, whereas the conformal measure $\Delta=1/3-P/\epsilon$ decreases substantially from approximately $0.208$ to $0.076$. This demonstrates that an approximately constant sound speed does not necessarily imply approximate conformality. The relativistic adiabatic index also increases sharply near the zero-pressure surface, reflecting the self-bound nature of the EOS.

papers.title: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
papers.abstract: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}\Sigma_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine. For $J^P=\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac32^-$ and pointlike constituents, the mean squared distances between the constituents of the three observed states are $0.85-0.47i$, $0.35-0.18i$ and $1.76-0.57i\,\mathrm{fm}^2$. Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4\mu_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $\mu_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,\mu_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,\mu_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.

papers.title: Analytic Two-Loop Classical Bremsstrahlung Amplitude in Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We compute the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges. Classical consistency suggests that two Coulomb exchanges dress the radiative tree amplitude. We show that this iteration accounts for the entire leading term and evaluate the resulting convolution. At fixed external transfer, the exchanges shift the momentum in the tree numerator, thereby changing the relative weights of its two polarization structures. We determine both coefficients at nonzero photon frequency and general relative velocity, with exact dependence on the spacetime dimension.

papers.title: Combining Pulsar Timing data with $MetaPulsar$. The linearized timing model
papers.abstract: Combining the data of multiple pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations increases the sensitivity to nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs) and other signals correlated between pulsars. The International PTA (IPTA) has combined such data, but historically these projects have taken many years. We introduce $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a software package that ingests the $\texttt{.par}$ and $\texttt{.tim}$ files of individual data releases, and turns them into single consistent deterministic models for the combined datasets, compatible with both timing packages $\texttt{PINT}$ and $\texttt{Tempo2}$. We validate the method in four ways. First, we show for two pulsars that the linearized timing solution of a combined dataset does not depend on the parameter values in the $\texttt{.par}$. A mild exception is formed by the Shapiro-delay parameters. No combination considered requires a manual refit. Second, for PSR J0613$-$0200 we show that the residuals are explained by the timing model if we take intrinsic red-noise and dispersion-measure processes into account, and that the single-PTA timing posteriors agree with one another and with the combination, except for the parallax. Third, we quantify the consistency of the timing parameters measured by different PTAs with a two-sample tension statistic, for every pulsar that is observed by multiple PTAs. Finally, we carry out a gravitational-wave background search on the direct combination of the NANOGrav 9-yr, EPTA DR1 (v2.2), and PPTA DR2 data releases, the constituents of IPTA Data Release 2 (DR2). The combined dataset is assembled in under two hours, and the recovered amplitude and spectral index of the common process are consistent with the published IPTA DR2 result. With $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a joint PTA analysis can be prototyped as soon as the individual collaborations publish their data, instead of after a years-long reprocessing effort.

papers.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
papers.abstract: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

papers.title: Testing general relativity with galaxy cluster clustering from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
papers.abstract: Deviations from general relativity on cosmological scales have been proposed as possible explanations for dark energy and dark matter. Galaxy cluster clustering offers an independent probe of gravitational growth, benefiting from theoretically motivated halo-bias constraints and complementing cluster-abundance measurements. We analyse a subsample of the largest publicly available spectroscopic galaxy cluster catalogue to date, constructed from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Following our selection cuts, the sample comprises 85 818 clusters at $0.1\leq z \leq0.4$ with $M_{\rm 500c}\gtrsim 6\times10^{13}\,M_\odot$. To enable a robust clustering analysis of this sample, we develop and validate methods for constructing random catalogues and calibrating the effective halo bias. We model the redshift-space two-point correlation function monopole and quadrupole over separations of $10$--$150\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ to jointly constrain gravitational growth and Alcock--Paczynski (AP) distortions, fixing the matter power-spectrum shape to that of a fiducial cosmology. We infer the product $f\sigma_8$ of the linear growth rate $f$ and the matter power spectrum normalisation $\sigma_8$, obtaining $f\sigma_8=0.45\pm0.08$ at an effective redshift of $z_{\rm eff}=0.28$, changing to $0.52\pm0.03$ when excluding baryon acoustic oscillation scales with tight AP priors. Both results are consistent with general relativity within the adopted fiducial cosmology.

papers.title: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
papers.abstract: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined. For finite $A, D, E$ type, the construction involves $q$-integers where $q=e^{\imath\pi/h}$ with $h$ the Coxeter number and there is a conjugate pair of $*$-preserving quantum Levi-Civita connections (QLCs). In the case of type $A$, these are necessarily contained in a previously known 1-parameter space of connections. For affine $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$ type, there is only one QLC, with real coefficients. Using the quantum Riemannian geometry, we construct a natural Einstein--Hilbert action and hence new quantum gravity models on $A_3,D_4,\widetilde D_4,\widetilde D_5,\widetilde D_6,\widetilde E_6$ in a functional integral approach, other than the 4-star $\widetilde D_4$ which we revisit.

papers.title: An Efficient Method for Directly Integrating the Vlasov Equation in Collisionless and Weakly-Collisional Simulations
papers.abstract: We describe and test a new numerical method to solve the Vlasov/Boltzmann equation in systems with arbitrary levels of collisionality. The method combines recent ideas to evolve the distribution function (DF) directly in 6+1 dimensional phase-space in a manner which is Lagrangian in both position+velocity. The 'particles' of traditional Monte-Carlo/Particle-In-Cell/N-body (MC/PIC/NB) methods become mesh-generating points defining a volume partition, each of which carries a set of momentum-Lagrangian basis functions representing a local anisotropic momentum DF. The DF is then integrated between cells and bases via a higher-order reconstruction and Godunov-type method, evolving a 10 or 13-moment representation of each basis to ensure manifest mass/momentum/energy conservation. The method allows one to represent arbitrary DFs, including multiple independent streams but also collisional or phase-mixed or thermal distributions (unlike traditional 'moments' or waterbag/tessellation methods), and the cost is bounded to a modest multiplier of MC/PIC/NB costs. We provide an example implementation which uses a spatially-Lagrangian volume partition, second-order reconstruction, and simple set of bases which ensure constant cell masses and couple directly to existing MC/PIC/NB machinery, made public in the code GIZMO. We validate in a series of test problems, demonstrating manifest conservation, Galilean and translation and rotation invariance, and ability to represent complex DFs without spurious dissipation or instability. We discuss applications where this method can have advantages compared to traditional algorithms for simulations of dark matter, stellar, weakly-collisional neutral gas, and particulate/dust dynamics; multiphase/polydisperse flows; cosmic ray and radiation transport/hydrodynamics; and plasma physics.

papers.title: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
papers.abstract: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
papers.abstract: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=\alpha\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $\alpha$ by construction, whereas increasing $\alpha$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$\alpha_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $\alpha$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-\kappa$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

papers.title: RevolIACT: a longitudinally distributed array of compact AI-driven Cherenkov telescopes for the time-domain sub-TeV sky
papers.abstract: Context. The coming decade will be the golden era of time-domain astronomy. In ten years, however, sensitive very-high-energy observations below ~1 TeV may be possible only at the two sites of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Each can observe a source for only a few hours per night. Aims. We quantify the loss caused by this limited coverage and assess whether RevolIACT, an array of compact stand-alone AI-driven stations, can close the gap. Methods. We estimate the sensitivity that a stand-alone station needs to detect important transients seen by current imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). We also compute the temporal coverage of layouts of ten to fourteen stations distributed in longitude, and how many of the 4401 Fermi-GBM gamma-ray bursts each layout could have observed when they occurred. Results. For each station, a sensitivity of ~15 % of the Crab flux in one hour above 0.2-0.3 TeV, about three times worse than that of current IACT systems, would suffice for an array to detect most of these transients. With the standard analysis, a telescope with a 5 m diameter mirror misses this target by a factor of 17. With a video vision transformer, it comes within a factor of two in an idealised simulation, and a 6 m telescope within 1.5. Ten to fourteen stations would provide three to four times the temporal coverage of CTAO, averaged over the sky and for the GBM bursts. Fourteen stations can observe most sources around the clock for about two months per year. Conclusions. Temporal coverage, not only flux sensitivity, will limit sub-TeV transient astronomy in the next decade. RevolIACT would complement CTAO. The concept relies on the transformer analysis, which is still young and will improve. The decisive next step is to confirm this performance on real data, with a prototype station.

papers.title: A transformer analysis lowers the energy threshold and improves the sensitivity of a compact imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope
papers.abstract: Context. A companion study simulated an idealised stand-alone imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope with a 5 m diameter mirror. A video vision transformer that processes the raw camera waveforms lowered its energy threshold by a factor of three, compared with the standard analysis based on image parameters. Aims. We use realistic photodetectors, compute the differential flux sensitivity, and study how hardware parameters affect the transformer analysis. Methods. With the simulation tools of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, we compare three photodetector efficiencies (100 %, 50 % and that of the LST-1 photomultipliers) with the transformer and with a standard analysis optimised for each. We then vary the dish diameter, field of view, pulse width and sampling rate. Results. With the LST-1 photomultipliers, the energy threshold is 0.18 TeV with the transformer and 0.73 TeV with the standard analysis. The standard analysis needs a photodetector efficiency of 100 % to match that threshold. The main reason is that the transformer works with events of about 35 photoelectrons in the camera, whereas the standard analysis needs about 200 before image cleaning. A 4 m dish with the transformer is more sensitive at all energies than a 5 m dish with the standard analysis. Dishes of 4, 5 and 6 m diameter give thresholds of 0.38, 0.18 and 0.13 TeV. Sampling the pixel signals at 2 GS/s instead of 5 GS/s raises the threshold to 0.26 TeV, whereas the single-photoelectron pulse width (1-3 ns) matters little. Conclusions. The analysis matters as much as the mirror area and the photodetector efficiency. With the transformer analysis, the idealised 5 m diameter telescope comes within a factor of about four of the sensitivity of LST-1 and MAGIC above 0.25 TeV, although its mirror area is 21 times smaller than that of the 23 m LST-1. This performance should improve substantially in the coming years.

papers.title: The long-period central star of planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
papers.abstract: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer period central stars are scarcer. We aim to characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455 which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We study archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We use long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, as well as derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. We find that the central binary of MPAJ1508-6455 has an orbital period of more than five years with a large eccentricity. The binary comprises a relatively low temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the nebular systemic velocity and inclination are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, the nebular abundance pattern adds support for a lower mass progenitor which did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of MPAJ1508-6455 is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

papers.title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
papers.abstract: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25. Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter. Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.

papers.title: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.abstract: Context. At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, $E_{\rm cyc}$, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models. Aims. We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at $L_{3-79}\simeq5\times10^{36}$, $4\times10^{35}$, and $6\times10^{34}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. We supplemented these data with Swift/XRT observations and performed broadband spectral analysis of all three states. Results. The high-luminosity spectrum follows a classical cutoff power law, whereas the intermediate- and low-luminosity spectra require two thermal Comptonization components to reproduce their two-hump shape. In the intermediate state, the cyclotron line, first reported at $\sim50$ keV in the high-luminosity state, lies on top of the high-energy hump. We interpret the low-luminosity state as representing stable accretion from a cold disk. IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.

papers.title: StochAXtic: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
papers.abstract: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

papers.title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'. We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.

papers.title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
papers.abstract: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 100 to 100,000 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. However, variations in stellar mass and disk size introduce substantial degeneracies, limiting the usefulness of individual line fluxes as tracers of external irradiation. We therefore assess all pairwise line flux ratios, which can significantly reduce these degeneracies, evaluating their correlation with the external field, the magnitude of their change across the FUV range, and predicted ALMA detectability. We identify 135 promising ratios, including several combining strong FUV sensitivity and high detectability with efficient single-tuning ALMA observations. The strongest diagnostics either contrast high- and low-excitation lines of the same or co-spatial species (e.g. CO J=8-7/J=1-0), probing different regions of the photoevaporative wind, or pair an FUV-sensitive wind tracer with comparatively insensitive emission arising closer to the disk (e.g. HCO+ J=3-2/C2H N=3-2). Our results provide a framework for identifying externally photoevaporating systems from spatially unresolved emission and constraining their incident FUV field strengths.

papers.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
papers.abstract: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

papers.title: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes
papers.abstract: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ay\'{o}n-Beato-Garc\'{i}a spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

papers.title: FastSpecFit: Spectrophotometric Modeling of 38 Million Extragalactic Targets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Second Data Release
papers.abstract: Optical spectrophotometry provides a direct window into the physical conditions, kinematics, and formation histories of galaxies and quasars. FastSpecFit is an open-source Python software package that forward-models each Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectrum jointly with its broadband photometry, convolving stellar-population synthesis and emission-line templates with each fiber's native spectral resolution. This forward-modeling approach preserves DESI's uncorrelated pixel statistics, fits a typical spectrum in ~0.1 s of single-core time, and scales to tens of millions of objects, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo resampling. FastSpecFit measures stellar velocity dispersions, non-parametric star-formation histories, stellar masses, star-formation rates, dust attenuation, K-corrections, rest-frame magnitudes, and fluxes and equivalent widths for 46 emission lines, including separate narrow and broad components for the Balmer lines. We describe these algorithms in detail, validate the measurements against independent codes, and present the resulting value-added catalog for DESI Data Release 2, which provides spectrophotometric and physical properties for 38 million extragalactic targets at 0<4. We also release a companion photometry-only catalog and document the catalogs previously released for the DESI Early Data Release and Data Release 1.

papers.title: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
papers.abstract: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density profiles without directly evolving the dust as a fluid. We compare the GRTM with dust profiles computed via standard methods using the $\texttt{FARGO3D}$ code, which models the dust as a pressureless fluid, and find very good agreement over a wide range of parameter space. Finally, we investigate how dust gap formation depends on the planet-to-star mass ratio ($q$) and Stokes number ($\mathrm{St}$), through a parameter study, establishing an empirical criterion for dust gap opening. In doing so, we have discovered a new regime of gap opening for small grains with $St \lesssim 10^{-2}$ and for planet mass well below Jupiter's, which is likely very relevant for gaps seen in ALMA images.

papers.title: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- The evolution of the radio-loud AGN fraction-stellar mass relation to $z3$ in the Euclid Deep Field North
papers.abstract: The incidence of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (RLAGN) and their energetic output via AGN feedback are crucial in understanding the evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure of the Universe. In the local Universe, the incidence of RLAGN has been shown to correlate strongly with host galaxy properties, particularly stellar mass. Using the large-area survey capabilities provided by Euclid and the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR), we present the first study of the RLAGN incidence--stellar mass relation to $z=3.0$. We perform a stringent analysis accounting for cross-matching reliability and stellar-mass incompleteness. In addition, we test the robustness of our results against AGN and host galaxy classification. This yields a sample of $3\,154$ RLAGN in the Euclid Deep Field North, comprising $2\,803$ low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs). We find that the LERG incidence as a function of stellar mass and radio luminosity follows a tight correlation over more than two orders of magnitude in stellar mass to $z=3.0$. The slope of the power-law relation decreases from $\gamma\approx2.5$ in the local Universe to $\gamma\approx1.0$ at $z=3.0$, indicating a relative increase in low-mass LERGs at earlier epochs. Separating the LERG population into actively star-forming and quiescent galaxies reveals that quiescent LERGs show a much steeper relation between incidence and stellar mass, with $\gamma\approx2.5$ compared to star-forming LERGs that show $\gamma\approx1.5$. However, the relation seems to be independent of whether galaxies are star-forming or quiescent at $z\geq2$, where both populations show relatively flat relations with $\gamma\approx1.0$. Our results suggest an evolutionary picture in which the LERG population transitions from cold-mode, merger-dominated accretion at earlier epochs to a scenario in which systems require a massive hot halo to fuel the AGN in the local Universe.

papers.title: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
papers.abstract: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.

papers.title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
papers.abstract: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $\alpha'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $\chi\bar\chi\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.

papers.title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
papers.abstract: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(\alpha, \delta)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

papers.title: How can every physicist become a Bohmian
papers.abstract: The Bohmian interpretation of quantum mechanics is controversial because it attributes deterministic trajectories to microscopic particles. We propose a reformulation that sidesteps this controversy: rather than applying Bohmian mechanics at the microscopic level, we recast it as an effective deterministic description of the macroscopic pointer of a measuring apparatus, with no claims about the fundamental nature of the microscopic world. In this form, the Bohmian trajectory becomes a practical tool for visualizing the emergence of a definite measurement outcome, broadly acceptable to physicists who would otherwise reject the Bohmian program.

papers.title: Time-Travel Paradox in a Bohmian Extension of Deutsch's Approach: Mandatory Tunneling as the "Banana Peel Mechanism"
papers.abstract: We consider a self-prevention paradox in which a particle travels through a wormhole into its own past, encounters its younger version, and blocks its movement. In a specially constructed one-dimensional model, this collision rules out a classically self-consistent history. Deutsch's quantum approach can resolve such contradictions by imposing a self-consistency condition on the density matrix. The physical interpretation of this approach, however, remains debated. In particular, Dunlap argues that Deutsch's model presupposes the existence of interacting parallel worlds. Here we extend Deutsch's approach within de Broglie-Bohm theory by supplementing the self-consistency condition on the quantum state with a self-consistency requirement for the particle's ontic configuration. This allows us to consider the self-consistent evolution of an individual particle. In a two-channel, narrow-band Gaussian approximation, we find a self-consistent solution in which quantum tunneling is mandatory, despite its arbitrarily small probability in an ordinary scattering process. This realizes the "banana peel mechanism": to avoid a contradiction during a journey into the past, an event that would ordinarily be extremely unlikely occurs nonetheless.

papers.title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-G\"ursey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $gg_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.

papers.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.abstract: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.

papers.title: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
papers.abstract: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. We show that incorporating the variability timescale improves mass recovery in the simulated sample and enhances agreement with the reference masses in the observed sample, achieving uncertainties of $\lesssim 0.5$ dex even with a single X-ray observation.

papers.title: Improved compensation for missing high-order aberrations with multi-frame blind deconvolution and phase diversity techniques
papers.abstract: Context. Image restoration with phase diversity (PD) and multi-frame blind deconvolution (MFBD) techniques lead to remarkable improvement in image quality, but is limited by the number of aberration parameters that can be determined. Compensation for the missing high-order modes is needed to further improve image quality, and to compensate for residual straylight. Aims. We aim to improve on methods for compensating missing high-order aberrations previously proposed by Scharmer et al. (2010) and Lofdahl & Hillberg (2022). Methods. The wavefront is divided into a set of low-order aberrations, which are treated individually, and high-order aberrations that are treated collectively. The high-order part of the transfer function is averaged, assuming Gaussian seeing statistics with Kolmogorov turbulence for the individual aberrations. Assuming that their accumulated effect is roughly uniform over the pupil, we obtain a high-order modulation transfer function that is represented with a single free parameter. Results. The high quality of the of the proposed high-order modulation transfer function is verified by calculating the Strehl from random samples of point-spread functions for D/r0 ranging from 4 to 20, where D is the telescope diameter and r0 the Fried seeing parameter. The proposed approximation offers significant advantages over the earlier proposals. Conclusions. The proposed method of compensating for missing high-order aberrations in PD or MFBD image reconstruction can dramatically improve the fidelity of solar images. Variations of the seeing (r0) within a data-set can be compensated for self consistently during PD or MFBD processing, but the average value of r0 must be provided from an external source. The computational cost of implementing this method is marginal.

papers.title: Solar atmospheric gravity wave phase differences: insights from MANCHA simulations and observations
papers.abstract: Phase-difference and coherence diagnostics are widely used to identify gravity waves in the solar atmosphere, but their sensitivity to opacity and radiative-transfer effects remains poorly understood. We investigate the robustness of gravity-wave signatures in velocity and temperature diagnostics and their appearance in spectroscopic observables. We perform k-/omega phase-difference and coherence analyses using three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations with the MANCHA code. Diagnostics are evaluated at constant geometrical heights and optical depths. Synthetic Fe I 6173 {\AA} profiles provide bisector velocities, continuum intensities, and line-core intensities. We also analyse high-resolution quiet-Sun observations from the 1-m Swedish Solar Telescope (SST). Velocity diagnostics show similar phase differences and coherence at both sampling levels, including those derived from synthetic and observed bisector velocities, indicating their relative insensitivity to the sampling method. In contrast, temperature diagnostics show stronger and more extended gravity-wave signatures at fixed geometrical height. Synthetic continuum and line-core intensities retain these signatures but exhibit phase differences more closely resembling temperature diagnostics at constant optical depth. SST observations show similar qualitative behaviour, despite quantitative differences. Our results demonstrate that Doppler velocity provides a relatively robust diagnostic of gravity-wave phase propagation, whereas temperature and intensity diagnostics are more sensitive to opacity and radiative-transfer effects. Consequently, the latter may introduce biases in estimates of wave propagation speeds and energy fluxes.

papers.title: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
papers.abstract: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.

papers.title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
papers.abstract: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. In this work we argue that in four-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity this constant is the Gauss--Bonnet contribution to the Wald entropy, and that it is carried by the normalization of the trace and not by the state. In particular, the conical expansion of the Gauss--Bonnet density is exactly linear in the deficit angle, and on smooth squashed cones it reduces to the intrinsic curvature of the cut, so that the term is a constant on every smooth cross-section and carries no boost energy. Its Noether charge is invariant under all deformations within a topological sector and central in any algebra that preserves the sector, and thus a state-independent constant on such an algebra can only rescale the trace. Additionally, when the boundary of the subregion is completed as the Euler action requires, the Gauss--Bonnet term does not contribute to the presymplectic form, the crossed product is inherited from Einstein gravity, and the constant is the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip. We state the hypotheses, we weaken factoriality to a central decomposition, and we illustrate the mechanism in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity and in topological black holes in anti-de Sitter space, where the topological weight displaces the Hawking--Page temperature and a black-hole merger shifts the coarse-grained boundary entropy by a state-independent amount.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves Population Study for Testing Kerr Hypothesis: Are Non-Kerr Deformations Universal or Source-Dependent?
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of binary black hole mergers can test the Kerr black hole hypothesis in the strong-field and dynamical regime. In our previous works, we constrained the deformation parameters $\alpha_{13}$ and $\epsilon_3$ of the Johannsen metric using individual inspiral-dominated events from GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 and found no evidence of deviations from the Kerr solution. Here we combine 17 of these events to test whether black holes are Kerr, share a common non-zero deformation, or have deformations that vary from source to source. We first estimate the Savage--Dickey Bayes factor of each event, and we test how it depends on the prior range and on the removal of single events. We then combine the event likelihoods assuming a universal deformation, yielding a tighter joint constraint. Next, we perform a simple hierarchical analysis by assuming that the event-level deformation parameters are drawn from a population with mean $\mu$ and intrinsic scatter $\sigma$. A universal deformation is constrained to $\alpha_{13}=-0.01^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $\epsilon_3=0.06^{+0.59}_{-0.54}$. The means from the population are consistent with zero for both parameters, and the scatter is not resolved by the current data. Our results are consistent with the Kerr hypothesis, but they cannot yet distinguish a shared deformation from a source-dependent one.

papers.title: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $\Omega_{gw}(f)/\Omega_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schr\"odinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless P\"oschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.

papers.title: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
papers.abstract: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|\beta_m|/|\beta_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

papers.title: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
papers.abstract: Using a high-resolution GRMHD simulation of a magnetically arrested disk, we investigate the physical mechanism driving magnetic-flux eruption. The horizon-threading magnetic flux declines mainly in off-equatorial regions, whereas localized hot spots associated with magnetic reconnection appear near the equatorial plane around the onset of flux decline. A non-axisymmetric, magnetically supported low-density structure, which we identify as a magnetic bubble, expands radially and azimuthally within a pre-existing low-density channel in the filamentary accretion flow. Based on these findings, we propose a physical picture linking reconnection, bubble expansion, and horizon magnetic flux decline. The reconnection occurs in the pre-existing low-density channel, and may reconfigure the field and promote bubble expansion. Magnetic-pressure gradients provide broadly distributed outward support for the expansion, while magnetic tension contributes a localized outward force near the equator. Bubble expansion may limit gas replenishment, helping to maintain the low-density region and reduce the total pressure near the equator. This pressure reduction may facilitate equatorward electromagnetic energy transport. In the simulation, the polar electromagnetic energy flux reverses from poleward to equatorward near the onset of the horizon-flux decline. The equatorward transport is concentrated in the bubble sector and carries electromagnetic energy from the off-equatorial magnetosphere to the equatorial region. This energy supply may sustain localized reconnection and plasma heating as the eruption develops.

papers.title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
papers.abstract: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincar\'e chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.

papers.title: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
papers.abstract: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. In this work, two novel DePFET technologies that address the two factors of the signal-to-noise ratio through fundamental changes to the intrinsic design are characterised: a buried-channel design aimed at reducing the limiting low-frequency noise by weakening the coupling between the channel and Si/SiO$_2$ interface traps, and a super-$g_q$ design intended to increase the charge gain by reducing the effective internal-gate capacitance. Their noise and energy resolution were mapped across the transistor bias space, over a wide temperature range (100-260 K) and for integration times of 0.4-9 $\mu$s (readout times of 2-19.2 $\mu$s per row), and compared with standard DePFETs as developed for the NewAthena Wide Field Imager (WFI). All three variants reach their lowest noise at about 155 K. The buried-channel device achieves an excellent equivalent noise charge (ENC) of 0.96 e$^-$ (at most 0.83 e$^-$ after subtracting the readout-electronics noise), demonstrating sub-electron noise over a complete 64$\times$64 DePFET matrix in a single readout, alongside a power consumption reduction of more than 50%. The super-$g_q$ DePFET shows a 2.6-fold increase in charge gain (about 1100 pA/e$^-$) but exhibits higher total noise due to an excess noise contribution. The results highlight the potential of the novel DePFETs, with the buried-channel technology offering immediate benefits for low-noise applications such as the WFI.

papers.title: Prescription for the rotational and orbital evolution of main-sequence binaries undergoing resonance locking
papers.abstract: In intermediate-mass binary stars, dynamical tides may play an important role in the orbital and rotational evolution of the system. One possible channel for long-term angular-momentum exchange is resonance locking, in which the evolution of the orbital and rotational parameters remains coupled to the evolution of the frequency of a resonantly excited oscillation mode. We aim to develop a simple prescription for describing the orbital and rotational evolution of binary systems undergoing resonance locking, and to assess the range of validity of this prescription. Using the asymptotic formalism for high-order gravity modes, we relate the temporal evolution of mode frequencies to the evolution of the orbital and rotational properties of the binary system. We then compare the resulting prescription with full integrations of the dynamical-tide evolution, including the contribution of multiple forcing frequencies. Depending on the type of resonance locking considered, we identify the regions of parameter space in which locking is expected to be possible in terms of orbital separation and rotation rate. We find that resonance locking is favoured in systems with significant spin-orbit asynchronism. When a locking is maintained, the proposed prescription reproduces the main features of the orbital and rotational evolution obtained from full dynamical-tide integrations, without requiring the explicit computation of the complete forcing-frequency spectrum. If resonance locking occurs, the evolution of the binary system can be described by a relatively simple prescription. Comparison with the observed population of binaries containing gamma-Doradus stars suggests that a significant fraction of the sample lies in regions compatible with the expected location of locked systems. Improved characterisation of these systems is required to distinguish resonance locking from alternative explanations.

papers.title: Inflation with an Exponential Power-Law Potential:Analytical Slow-Roll Relations, Branch Dynamics, and Conditional Reheating Matching
papers.abstract: We study canonical single-field inflation driven by the potential $V(\phi)=M^4\exp(\phi/M_{\rm Pl})(1+k\phi/M_{\rm Pl})^{-1/k}$ with $k<0$. We retain the canonical Einstein--scalar action and derive analytical relations within the slow-roll approximation. Expressing the local spectra through the logarithmic slope $A=kx/(1+kx)$, with $x=\phi/M_{\rm Pl}$, yields an endpoint-independent consistency relation among the scalar tilt, tensor ratio, and running at their stated approximation orders. On the negative-field branch, an exact phase-space argument shows that an initially downhill, inflationary hilltop trajectory cannot end inflation within the bare single-field model. We specify the endpoint as a phenomenological input and use a Lambert-$W$ solution of the slow-roll e-fold integral. Tables and figures illustrate the fixed choice $x_e=-2$ and must be interpreted conditionally on a completion that implements this endpoint and preserves the adiabatic spectrum. The reheating-matching relation uses explicit scale and thermal conventions and imposes both endpoint energy bounds and nonnegative reheating duration. The observational comparison uses published marginalized intervals rather than reconstructed joint posteriors. These results establish local analytical structure and conditional numerical benchmarks. A complete exit mechanism, a unique reheating equation of state, and precision spectral predictions remain unestablished.

papers.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

papers.title: A comprehensive Sun-as-a-star catalog of interplanetary type-III bursts: Statistics and a framework for stellar exospace weather applications
papers.abstract: Decameter-hectometric (DH) type-III bursts, produced by energetic electron beams escaping into interplanetary (IP) space, are often associated with strong soft X-ray (SXR) flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle events (SEPEs). With future DH missions being planned, these intense bursts could provide reliable exospace weather event diagnostics, given the lack of direct stellar IP particle and CME probes. We present a catalog of DH type-III bursts associated with 538 out of 734 $\geq$C5-class flares observed by Wind and STEREO spacecraft during 2006-2025. Independent of the SXR flare strength, the occurrence and Sun-as-a-star emission properties of DH type-III bursts distinguish confined flares, CMEs with and without strong IP shocks, and SEPEs. We find that logistic-regression models combining SXR and type-III properties provide more accurate and well-calibrated CME/SEPE occurrence probabilities than a model based only on SXR parameters. Further, a space weather event probability-estimation model based on physically meaningful, scale-free parameters derived from SXR and type-III properties outperforms an SXR parameter-only model. This result presents a way to define solar-calibrated exospace weather prediction models extendable to stellar flares with a range of energy scales but similar underlying physics. We also present a catalog of 26 shock-associated type-III (S-type-III) bursts that appear to start from cotemporal DH type-II bursts and are generally associated with fast halo CMEs and major SEPEs. Our catalogs and the scale-free model form a benchmark for exospace weather studies.
